question: Source for every street in Montana with names, drawn by the site from its own per-tile JSON (no tile server, Leaflet only).
bottom_line: Recommend the Census TIGER/Line 2025 All Roads county files as the one source for the first build: of the two candidates checked, the only one with a clear legal basis (a Census statement that its work is not copyrighted, plus a citation request). Its geometry agrees with the Montana State Library road file to a median of 0.9 m in the Billings tile. The gap is names: 23 to 55 percent of vehicular features have no name in the three counties measured, so unnamed streets will show without labels. The state file names almost every road (blank on 0.13 percent of records) but carries only a disclaimer, so it is not cleared for publication until the Library confirms reuse in writing. Simplified at 2 m, the statewide TIGER vehicular lines are about 69 MB (range 58 to 77) of 5-decimal JSON, against about 170 MB (range 161 to 177) before simplification; these are estimates from three counties. Measured statewide for the state file: before simplification 171.4 MB, at 2 m 48.8 MB, at 5 m 32.7 MB (vehicular classes; one-array polyline format).

recommendation.pick: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2025 All Roads, the 56 Montana county files (88,860,450 bytes zipped), as the single source for the first build
recommendation.why: It is the only candidate with a clear, checked legal basis (the Census statement that its work is not copyrighted, with a citation request and a trademark rule). It covers local streets, alleys, frontage and private service roads, and it agrees with the state file to a median of 0.9 m in Billings. Its weakness is names: 23 to 55 percent of vehicular features are unnamed in the three counties measured.
recommendation.legal_basis: Title 17 U.S.C. 105 as stated in the Census technical documentation section 1.2 (Copyright protection is not available for any work of the United States Government). The file metadata says the files are free to use in a product or publication with acknowledgement. Attribution text on the About page; no TIGER/Line name in product names; no accuracy claim.
classes_to_draw: S1400 local neighborhood road, rural road, city street
S1740 service road for access to industrial, ranch, resource extraction
classes_left_out: S1750 internal Census use (outside the list; open question)
S1780 parking lot road (outside the list)

S1830 bridle path (not in these counties)
recommendation.names: Use FULLNAME where it is not blank. Leave unnamed features unlabelled. Do not name a road from a neighboring county or from another source unless the terms allow it.
recommendation.dedupe: Drop exact duplicate geometries before tiling (117, 39, 131 records in the three counties); keep one record and carry its name if it has one.
recommendation.simplify: Douglas-Peucker in metres at 2 m for the detail tiles (validated: maximum deviation 1.998 m on 1,242 Billings pieces); 5 m as the coarser option. Coordinates at 5 decimals.

terms.source: Census TIGER/Line Shapefile Technical Documentation 2025, section 1.2 Citation Information
terms.quote: Copyright protection is not available for any work of the United States Government (Title 17 U.S.C., Section 105). Thus, you are free to reproduce census materials as you see fit. We would ask, however, that you cite the Census Bureau as the source.
terms.reading: The Census Bureau states that its work is not copyrighted under 17 U.S.C. 105 and asks for a citation. This is the strongest TIGER terms statement found. It does not use the words public domain.

terms.source: Census TIGER/Line Shapefile Technical Documentation 2025, section 1.1 TIGER/Line Shapefile Legal Disclaimers
terms.quote: TIGER/Line® is a registered trademark of the Census Bureau. TIGER/Line cannot be used as or within the proprietary product names of any commercial product including or otherwise relevant to Census Bureau data and may only be used to refer to the nature of such a product. The Census Bureau requests that any repackaging of the TIGER/Line Shapefile data, documentation, and other files accompanying it for distribution include a conspicuously placed statement to this effect on the product's cover, the first page of the website, or elsewhere of comparable visibility.
terms.reading: Do not use TIGER/Line in a product name. The site should add a visible statement about the source on its About page (the request asks for one on repackaged data).

terms.source: Census TIGER/Line Shapefile Technical Documentation 2025, section 1.1 (no warranty)
terms.quote: No warranty, expressed or implied, is made with regard to the accuracy of the data in the TIGER/Line Shapefiles, and no liability is assumed by the United States Government in general, or the Census Bureau specifically, as to the positional or attribute accuracy of the data.
terms.reading: No accuracy promise from the source. The site must say so and must not present TIGER geometry as surveyed.

terms.source: Census TIGER/Line Shapefile Technical Documentation 2025, section 1.3 Contact Information
terms.quote: Members of the public can obtain the TIGER/Line Shapefiles free of charge through the Census Bureau’s website
terms.reading: Free of charge to the public; the download is the public source.

These products are free to use in a product or publication, however acknowledgement must be given to the U.S. Census Bureau as the source. No warranty, expressed or implied is made with regard to the accuracy of the spatial accuracy, and no liability is assumed by the U.S. Government in general or the U.S. Census Bureau, specifically as to the spatial or attribute accuracy of the data. The TIGER/Line Shapefiles may not be suitable for high-precision measurement applications such as engineering problems, property transfers, or other uses that might require highly accurate measurements of the earth's surface.Coordinates in the TIGER/Line shapefiles have six implied decimal places, but the positional accuracy of these coordinates is not as great as the six decimal places suggest.
terms.reading: Same statement as the technical document, in the file's own metadata. 'free to use in a product or publication' with acknowledgement required. Not a license grant; it restates the Census statement with an acknowledgement request.

terms.source: Yellowstone County roads ISO 19115 metadata, element Use Constraints (last sentence)
terms.quote: The TIGER/Line Shapefiles may not be suitable for high-precision measurement applications such as engineering problems, property transfers, or other uses that might require highly accurate measurements of the earth's surface.
terms.reading: Not for property or engineering measurement; the site must not state property boundaries from these lines.

terms.source: Census TIGER/Line Shapefile Technical Documentation 2025, section 3.3.6 Coordinates
terms.quote: Coordinates in the TIGER/Line Shapefiles have six decimal places, but the positional accuracy of these coordinates may not be as great as the six decimal places suggest. The spatial accuracy varies with the source materials used.
terms.reading: Six decimals do not mean six decimals of accuracy. No accuracy figure is given; this record uses the cross-source comparison instead.

terms.quote: The All Roads shapefiles will contain multiple overlapping road segments where a segment is associated with more than one road feature.
terms.reading: Coincident duplicates are by design in All Roads. Deduplicate geometry before tiling (exact duplicates measured: 117, 39 and 131 records in the three counties).

open_questions: MSL reuse terms (decisive for the name source): the metadata has only a disclaimer and no license, credit or redistribution statement, and it aggregates tribal, county, city and federal data. Ask Montana State Library (geoinfo@mt.gov, 406-444-5354) in writing whether the site may publish derived tiles with names, and whether contributing agencies add terms. Unverified until answered.

Names gap in the recommended source: FULLNAME is blank on 25.6% of Yellowstone records, 54.8% of Judith Basin records and 39.0% of Lincoln records (vehicular: 23.2%, 54.6%, 38.8%). Owner decision: leave unnamed roads unlabelled (recommended here) or add a label rule. Other open sources for names were not checked in this record (for example state highway data or OpenStreetMap, which would need its own terms review and live check).

Coverage: neither source covers every street alone. In the Billings tile 5.9% of TIGER vehicular vertices have no state-file line within 20 m (frontage roads S1640 at 78% of their vertices, private service roads S1740 at 89%, unnamed streets), and 2.4% of state-file Local vertices have no TIGER line within 20 m (subdivision streets such as Madrid Drive). A union needs a dedupe and conflict rule.

TIGER class S1750 ('Internal U.S. Census Bureau use') is outside the requested class list: 198 features (2.9%) in Yellowstone, 8 in Judith Basin, 57 in Lincoln, all blank-named in Yellowstone. Contents not examined; excluded here.
TIGER class S1780 (parking lot roads, 23 features in Yellowstone) is outside the requested list; excluded here. TIGER S1710, S1720, S1820 (walkway, stairway, bike path) excluded as requested.

State file class 'Other' (15,416 records, 6.0%): defined as 'Other is any road or path type that does not fit into the above categories.' Excluded here; its contents were not examined, so it may hide drivable roads.
TIGER FULLNAME 'Internal' appears on 73 Yellowstone features and on 136 unmatched Billings vertices; meaning not verified.

Duplicates: exact duplicate geometries are 117 (Yellowstone), 39 (Judith Basin) and 131 (Lincoln) records in All Roads. The state file has overlaps by its own description; its duplicate count was not fully measured (a first-part hash only).

Positional accuracy: neither source publishes a positional accuracy figure in the documents checked. Measured agreement in the Billings tile: TIGER vertices to state-file lines median 0.9 m, p95 36 m (the tail is the unmatched roads); 27th Street centerlines differ by a median 6.3 m (p95 8.4 m). Simplification tolerance of 2 to 5 m is below the 27th Street disagreement, so it adds little error relative to the source.

Datum: TIGER is NAD83 and is used as WGS84 without change. The state file is NAD83(2011) State Plane and was converted with pyproj without a datum grid. The NAD83 to WGS84 offset was not measured here (unverified; commonly stated as about 1 m or less in the conterminous US).

Address ranges: the TIGER All Roads file has no address range fields (LINEARID, FULLNAME, RTTYP, MTFCC only). The state file has FromAddr and ToAddr fields. The typed-address search (B3) needs address ranges from another product (TIGER address features were not checked) or from the state file under its terms.

Tile sizes: the statewide TIGER tile sizes are from three counties only. Lincoln County tiles are about 2 to 3 times the Yellowstone tiles (largest 416 KB before simplification, 157 KB at 2 m). The Billings tile is 497 KB before simplification and 148 KB at 2 m for TIGER. The state file is measured statewide: its largest 0.1 degree tile (centre 48.2 N, 114.3 W, the Kalispell area by coordinates) is 1.43 MB before simplification and 345 KB at 2 m, and its median tile is 22 KB before and 4.3 KB at 2 m. A per-tile byte budget is not set here.

State file pieces: the Billings tile has 4,128 pieces against 1,340 TIGER pieces, because the state file breaks lines at address changes (inferred from the per-piece ranges). Merging consecutive pieces of one street at shared endpoints was not measured and could cut the per-piece overhead.

Zoom and tolerance: the pixel figures are computed from the Web Mercator resolution at 45.8 N and were not rendered in a browser. At zoom 17 a 2 m tolerance is 2.4 px and a 5 m tolerance 6 px; at zoom 18 they are 4.8 px and 12 px. The owner should choose the tolerance per zoom band after a browser check (rule 8).

Freshness: TIGER/Line 2025 (metadata date 2025-09-18, citation publication 2025-10); the release cadence was not checked here. The state file was exported 2026-09-30; the ReadMe says the export is monthly and the metadata says the update is as needed; a refresh schedule is not set.
RTTYP blank on 1,740 Yellowstone records, same count as the blank FULLNAME; meaning of the blank code not verified.
Not checked in this record: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Montana Department of Transportation road inventories, and any commercial source. None is recommended here.
